institution: Rytmisk Musikkonservatorium (RMC / Rhythmic Music Conservatory)
program: Master of Music (MMus) in Music Creation
qualification: cand. musicae (Music Creation) / Master of Music (MMus) (Music Creation)
accreditationStatus: Independent institution of higher education under the Danish Ministry of Culture; the only Danish conservatoire specialising in contemporary/rhythmic music
language: Danish is the default; "The entrance exam is usually held in Danish but can be conducted in English." Applications accepted in Danish, Norwegian, Swedish and English. Teaching language for the programme itself is UNVERIFIED but in practice RMC teaches international students in English.
whatYouStudy: Artistic Development Practice (30 ECTS) — developing compositional/songwriting material and reflecting on it; Music Creation (10 ECTS) — composition, instrumentation, arrangement, lyrics and TECHNOLOGY; Entrepreneurship (10 ECTS); Electives (10 ECTS); External Integrated Module (30 ECTS) — a real project outside RMC with cultural/music partners; Master Project (30 ECTS) ending in a public concert at RMC graduation festival. Approx. 8 students admitted per year.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: applicants must have "completed a Bachelor degree in music from RMC, a relevant Bachelor degree in music from another Danish music conservatory, or a relevant Bachelor degree in music from a foreign music conservatory", or "expect to have completed an eligible Bachelor degree by 1 July 2026 at the latest". Plus: "Based on a specific assessment, the conservatory may recognise other artistically based Bachelors degrees in music as qualifying."
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY / DOUBTFUL on paper but the artistic bar is instrument-free. The qualifying-degree clause is music-only: "Based on a specific assessment, the conservatory may recognise other artistically based Bachelors degrees in music as qualifying" — note it still says "in music". HOWEVER RMC explicitly removes the performer barrier: "Applicants do not need to participate as a musician/singer in the music examples in their portfolio, and it is not a requirement to be able to play an instrument - the conservatory also accepts applicants who work exclusively on computers." A BSc Software Engineering would need a dispensation on the degree requirement — UNVERIFIED whether RMC grants this.
portfolioSpec: EXACT (Round 1): "2-3 music examples" composed, arranged AND produced by the applicant, total duration "10 min.", mp3 format. Optional sheet music / graphic notation / text as pdf. HARD CONSTRAINT: "A minimum of one-third of the music submitted in your portfolio must be composed for and performed by others." Supplementary text: max 500 keystrokes per music example on the creation process, max 250 keystrokes per music example on roles. "All material must be composed, arranged and produced by you. Co-writes are not permitted." Round 1 scored out of 100; minimum 40/100 to advance. RMC selects two to three times as many applicants for round 2 as it admits.
auditionSpec: TWO ROUNDS. Round 1 is portfolio-only, no attendance. Round 2 is an IN-PERSON exam at RMC in Copenhagen, approx. 25 minutes: 10 min work presentation (live performance, recording, OR a combination — a recording alone is permitted, so no instrument is strictly needed), 5 min oral presentation of working methods, 10 min interview. Max 5 musicians including sound engineer if performing live. NOT a classical performance audition and NOT an ear-training test — it is a portfolio defence with an optional live element. CRITICAL LOGISTICS: "Exams cannot be conducted via video streaming unless explicitly stated for a specific programme" — so a Schengen visit visa and travel to Copenhagen is likely required for Round 2.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 10,000 per year for the Master programme (EUR 20,000 total for 120 ECTS). Bachelor is EUR 11,000/yr and APD EUR 9,000/yr for comparison.
otherFees: Application fee DKK 600 per programme (non-refundable after the deadline). Danish living costs plus the Round-2 travel to Copenhagen.
totalCostEstimate: EUR 20,000 tuition + DKK 600 application + Copenhagen living (Danish study-visa self-support requirement, UNVERIFIED 2027 figure) + round-2 travel. Roughly EUR 45,000-50,000 over two years.
scholarshipName: No RMC scholarship found for non-EU students
scholarships: The RMC tuition page lists only EXEMPTIONS, not scholarships: "an exception is made for students who participate in: An Erasmus Mundus programme, A Fulbright or DIS programme, Other bilateral agreements", plus exemptions for foreign students with permanent Danish residency and for those under the Afghan-assistance or Ukrainian-refugee acts. NONE of these is available to an ordinary Tunisian applicant. The Danish Government Scholarship scheme (Kulturministeriet / Danish state tuition waivers and scholarships for highly qualified non-EU students) is administered per-institution; whether RMC receives an allocation is UNVERIFIED — worth a direct email to rmc@rmc.dk.
languageRequirement: Application may be in English. Entrance exam can be conducted in English on request. Teaching language UNVERIFIED.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — no English test requirement stated on the admission page.
deadline: 3 February 2026 at 12:00 CET — PRIOR CYCLE. For a September 2027 intake expect approx. 3 February 2027. UNVERIFIED.

scopeNote: IN SCOPE but composition/songwriting-weighted. The portfolio must be "composed, arranged and produced by you", and RMC explicitly welcomes applicants "who work exclusively on computers" — so it is a real route for a bedroom/DAW producer. It is not a mixing-and-mastering engineering degree. CONFIRMED: RMC has NO master-level Music Production specialisation — Music Production at RMC is a 180-ECTS BACHELOR only (Music Production 50 ECTS, Music Technology 20, Music Pedagogy 20, Composition/Arrangement/Production/Analysis 20, Art and Culture Studies 10, Bachelor Project 20). That bachelor is notable as a fallback because "Anyone can apply for the Bachelor programme in Music Production" with no specific background needed and no requirement to perform — but it is a second bachelor, not a master, and its portfolio requires that "at least two of the uploaded music examples must be productions where you have produced music for someone other than yourself" (Portfolio A: 2-3 examples, 7-8 min; Portfolio B: 3-4 examples, 10-11 min; plus a 3-year activity overview). RMC master list confirmed as: Music Creation, Music Education, Music Performance, Music Performance - Nordic Master: The Composing Musician.

The following bachelor’s degrees are pre-approved: Bachelor’s degree from a music academy; Bachelor’s degree from another artistic programme approved by the Danish Ministry of Culture*; Bachelor’s degree from a university musicology programme*" with the footnote "*The applicant may have to pass an extended admission test to verify that he/she possesses the skills, knowledge, or qualifications that are acquired on music academy bachelor programmes but which the applicant may not have acquired on his/her qualifying BA programme. acceptsNonMusic: NO on the pre-approved list, and this is the honest read. The three pre-approved categories are all music/artistic degrees: "Bachelor’s degree from a music academy", "Bachelor’s degree from another artistic programme approved by the Danish Ministry of Culture", "Bachelor’s degree from a university musicology programme". A BSc Software Engineering is none of these. The list says these are "pre-approved", implying other degrees may be individually assessed, but the PDF does not state a dispensation route. UNVERIFIED whether RAMA will individually assess a non-music BSc. NOTE the extended-admission-test footnote covers ear training and music theory for non-conservatoire entrants — a real risk for this candidate.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: "15-20 minutes of audio featuring works produced by the applicant. Some of the works may have been created in cooperation with others; if so, the application must clearly state who did what. The applicant is encouraged to demonstrate artistic coherence and at the same time a degree of variation". Plus a "work description: A text that briefly (maximum of two A4 pages) explains the background of the music and how it was created. Information about production location, equipment used, and any other participants must be clear"; a "CV with a particular emphasis on the applicant’s music production experience"; and the "diploma for qualifying bachelor’s degree". Audio format not specified in the PDF (UNVERIFIED).
auditionSpec: THIS IS A PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST, NOT A PERFORMANCE AUDITION — the single most important distinction for this candidate, and RAMA is the clearest example of it in the region. VERBATIM: "No later than 8 days prior to the admission te[s]t, the applicants receive a production assignment. The completed assignment is presented during the admission test." Test structure: total maximum 30 minutes. "Presentation (10 minutes maximum): The completed assignment is played back, and the applicant gives a presentation accounting for e.g. production methods and artistic intentions." "Interview (20 minutes maximum)" covering artistic profile, technical and artistic aspects of the application and the production assignment, "the applicant’s work methods including use of software/hardware et cetera", music production and music industry experience, background and previous education, and ambitions for the programme. Graded on: "A) The submitted works B) The presentation C) Suitability for study based on the interview and the written material submitted". NO instrument required, NO ear-training test at the master admission test itself — but the qualifying-degree footnote warns an "extended admission test" covering ear training/music theory may be imposed on non-music-academy entrants. Admission tests are scheduled for January and February. Whether the test can be taken remotely is UNVERIFIED.
tuitionNonEU: DKK 114,578 per year (two semesters) for master programmes, approx. EUR 15,380/yr — so approx. DKK 229,156 / EUR 30,760 for the 2-year master. (For reference the RAMA Aalborg bachelor in Electronic Sound and Music is quoted at EUR 6,600 per term on studyindenmark.dk.)
otherFees: Application fee DKK 500 for master applicants, non-refundable unless withdrawn before the 1 December deadline. Applicant must pay all costs for any accompanists/bands (not applicable to this programme). Travel to Aarhus/Aalborg for the admission test in January/February.
totalCostEstimate: Approx. DKK 229,700 (EUR 30,800) tuition + Danish living costs over 2 years + admission-test travel. Danish study-permit self-support requirement for 2027 UNVERIFIED.
scholarships: VERBATIM exemption clause: "students who enrol the academy as part of an official exchange programme i.e. Erasmus or Nordplus or a Bilateral Agreement are exempted from the tuition fee" — not available to a direct-entry Tunisian degree student. The Danish state operates a scheme of tuition waivers and scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students distributed through institutions; whether RAMA has an allocation and whether it reaches this new Aalborg programme is UNVERIFIED. institution: Taideyliopiston Sibelius-Akatemia / Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki (Uniarts Helsinki)
program: Music Technology, master (Musiikkiteknologia) — specialisation path RECORDING ARTS
accreditationStatus: State university (Taideyliopisto / University of the Arts Helsinki), Sibelius Academy is its music faculty
language: TRI-LINGUAL AND THIS IS THE KEY FACT: "The languages of tuition in the Music Technology programme are Finnish, Swedish, and English." "the status of English is very pronounced within the Music Technology programme." Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in ONE of the three.
durationEcts: 2.5 years (150 ECTS equivalent). Admits new students on ALTERNATING years — either a 5.5-year bachelor+master cohort or a 2.5-year master-only cohort.
whatYouStudy: Three specialisation paths. (1) RECORDING ARTS — the in-scope one: students develop expertise in "music producer and sound engineer" roles, covering recording, editing and mixing techniques for both popular AND classical music, plus live sound reinforcement and audio technology. (2) Film and Game Music — music production for film, game and visual media, music design, sound design, composing and arranging for virtual instruments. (3) Creative Electronic Music Practices — electroacoustic, live electronics, sonic arts, sound installation, generative music (OUT OF SCOPE per brief). Students participate in recording Sibelius Academy concerts and in contemporary-music, multimedia and electroacoustic concert production.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: applicants need "at least one of the following: A lower university degree in music (Bachelor), a university of applied sciences degree in music, a foreign degree or qualification in music", or a non-music degree with supplementary music studies. Programme-specific clause VERBATIM: "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies."
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONDITIONALLY, AND THIS IS THE BEST NON-MUSIC CLAUSE FOUND IN THE WHOLE REGION. QUOTE: "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies." A BSc Software Engineering is a higher education degree in the field of technology. The binding condition is "a sufficient amount of music studies", which is not quantified on the page (UNVERIFIED how many ECTS of music study count). This clause exists specifically because Music Technology expects engineers — it is a designed door for exactly this candidate profile, provided he accumulates formal music studies before applying.
portfolioSpec: EXACT advance assignments: (1) Portfolio of MAXIMUM 3 WORKS, total length 10 MINUTES OR LESS, audio in MP3 or video in MP4 format. (2) Video self-presentation, 3 minutes or less. (3) Project description forms (PDF). (4) Motivation letter, max 2 A4 pages. (5) CV (PDF). (6) Final project plan, max 2 A4 pages. (7) Preliminary study plan (max 150 ECTS credits). Advance assignments are weighted 100%.
auditionSpec: THERE IS A PERFORMANCE AUDITION — this is the decisive distinction for this candidate and it counts AGAINST him. The remote examination has two parts: (1) "Instrument or voice audition (7-10 minutes) - any tradition welcome" weighted 40%; (2) "Interview (up to 25 minutes)" discussing portfolio, audition, background and plans, weighted 60%. So a live instrumental or vocal performance of 7-10 minutes IS required, although any musical tradition is accepted. NO ear-training or music-theory test is mentioned in the documentation. GOOD NEWS: the examination is REMOTE — no travel to Helsinki needed.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 0 IF STUDYING IN FINNISH OR SWEDISH. EUR 28,000 per academic year if studying in English, for students starting 1 August 2026 or later. THIS IS THE FINNISH-LANGUAGE LOOPHOLE THE BRIEF ASKED ABOUT AND IT IS REAL. Uniarts states VERBATIM: "Tuition fees at Uniarts Helsinki are applicable to bachelor and master students who study in English and who are not citizens of EU, EEA, or Switzerland" and "If a student’s language of studies changes to Finnish or Swedish, they will no longer have to pay annual tuition fees." Finnish national law only permits fees for vieraskielinen (foreign-language) degree education; Finnish- and Swedish-taught degrees are free of charge regardless of nationality. Music Technology is one of the very few Sibelius Academy programmes that formally offers Finnish, Swedish AND English as tuition languages, so the exemption is genuinely reachable here rather than theoretical.
otherFees: EUR 100 application fee for applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland. Language test must be completed by the stated date if proficiency is not evidenced by prior studies.
totalCostEstimate: If admitted in Finnish/Swedish: EUR 0 tuition + EUR 100 application + Helsinki living costs (Finnish residence-permit maintenance requirement approx. EUR 800/month, UNVERIFIED 2027 figure) — roughly EUR 24,000 over 2.5 years, all living costs. If admitted in English: add EUR 70,000 tuition over 2.5 years with NO scholarship available.
scholarships: VERBATIM: "The university does not grant any scholarships to cover the tuition fee for students starting in August 2026 or later" and "Uniarts Helsinki does not grant scholarships for living expenses." The ONLY way to make this affordable is the Finnish/Swedish language exemption.
languageRequirement: Must demonstrate proficiency in Finnish, Swedish OR English by the application deadline, through prior studies or a standardised test. To get the fee exemption the language of studies must be Finnish or Swedish — which means real Finnish (or Swedish) proficiency, realistically B2/C1, achieved before applying. UNVERIFIED exact required level.
englishTest: Accepted as one of the three qualifying languages; exact test/score UNVERIFIED. Note: choosing English triggers the EUR 28,000/yr fee.
deadline: *** NO INTAKE IN 2027 *** VERBATIM from the programme page: "No admission in 2027. Next possible time to apply will be announced later." The programme admits every other year. whatYouStudy: Five specialisations: four performance-based (Performing Music, ELECTRONIC MUSIC, World Music, Songwriting) and one theoretical (Music Business and Management). The Electronic Music specialisation is performance-oriented and "guides students in discovering and enabling their artistic ideas through the use of music technology". The curriculum combines artistic development with popular musicology: "a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between performance practice and relevant popular musicology" plus an academic foundation. "Rhythmic music" is UiA’s Scandinavian term for popular music (pop, rock, folk, jazz).
entryRequirements: VERBATIM/near-verbatim: general admission is a bachelor’s degree or equivalent of at least three years (180 credits), "The admission criteria must include a specialisation unit of at least 80 credits in performing music or equivalent", with at least 20 credits at level 2 in the specialisation unit. Performance specialisations require "a very high level on the principal instrument" plus music theory knowledge equivalent to the Scientific Theory, Aesthetics and Analysis courses. Applicants "must write a proposal for a project description for a master’s thesis according to the guidelines laid down for the Faculty of Arts", submitted five weeks before the entrance exam.
acceptsNonMusic: NO. The 80-credit specialisation unit in performing music is mandatory. A BSc Software Engineering supplies none. Combined with "a very high level on the principal instrument", this is closed to this candidate.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — the programme page describes an entrance examination rather than an uploaded portfolio. A master’s thesis project description must be submitted five weeks before the entrance exam.
auditionSpec: PERFORMANCE AUDITION — DISQUALIFYING FOR THIS CANDIDATE. Ranking is by entrance examination in two equally weighted halves: "Audition: Scored 10–20 points; minimum 10 required to advance (50% of total score)" and "Interview: Scored 10–20 points (50% of total score)". Performance specialisations, including Electronic Music, require "a very high level on the principal instrument". This is a playing audition, not a production test.

institution: Eesti Muusika- ja Teatriakadeemia (EAMT / Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre)
program: Composition and Music Technology (MA) — Helilooming ja muusikatehnoloogia — specialisation RECORDING ARTS / helirežii
accreditationStatus: Public state university of music and theatre, Estonia
language: ENGLISH-TAUGHT for international students — the MA is on EAMT’s list of master’s programmes available to international students (alongside Jazz Music MA, Contemporary Improvisation MA, CoPeCo, Contemporary Physical Performance Making). Estonian-taught study is also possible.
durationEcts: UNVERIFIED exact ECTS — Estonian MA norm is 120 ECTS / 2 years. Not stated on the pages fetched.
whatYouStudy: Four specialisation strands: classical composition, electroacoustic composition, audiovisual composition, and RECORDING ARTS. Recording Arts is "the only place to study classical music recording in Estonia"; teaching runs in collaboration with Estonian Public Broadcasting (ERR) and the Estonian National Symphony Orchestra, with the opportunity to learn pop and jazz recording under leading practitioners, using top-level technical equipment and mixing rooms. Students are "not constrained by strict academic restrictions" and may work with multiple professors across aesthetics. The COMMUTE festival each spring connects students with the international professional music world.
entryRequirements: A completed bachelor’s degree, proof of English language proficiency, and passing the specialisation entrance exam. Exact verbatim academic prerequisite for Recording Arts UNVERIFIED — the admission page states the portfolio and exam criteria but not a required bachelor field.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED BUT PROMISING — no clause on the admission page restricts entry to holders of a music bachelor. The admission page for Recording Arts specifies only portfolio content and exam criteria; the general international page requires "Previous educational credentials with grades" and "Proof of English language Proficiency". Because the Recording Arts entrance exam grades a submitted recording rather than a degree, an applicant with a strong portfolio and a non-music BSc has a plausible case. MUST BE CONFIRMED with admissions@eamt.ee — no quotable sentence either way.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: submit 10 MINUTES of self-produced recorded music with detailed explanatory notes; the portfolio MUST INCLUDE BOTH AN ACOUSTIC RECORDING AND AN OVERDUB RECORDING; plus a list of works demonstrating sound engineering and composition experience. (Note: the acoustic-recording requirement means he cannot submit an all-in-the-box electronic portfolio — he needs at least one real-room, microphone-based recording.)
auditionSpec: PRACTICAL/TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT PLUS COLLOQUIUM — NOT a performance audition and NOT an ear-training test. The entrance exam evaluates: "Sound quality reflective of AES/EBU standards, Originality, Technique, Musicality, Knowledge of musical styles, Creative personality, General knowledge of music and culture", and the candidate must "converse on a variety of topics reflecting professional competence and knowledge of culture and society (colloquium)". Graded 0-10 points with 5 the minimum pass. NOTE the explicit AES/EBU engineering standard — this is judged as an engineer’s work. VIDEO/REMOTE POSSIBLE: EAMT permits entrance by video recording, but only "if the examination panel has no doubts about authenticity of the recording, the quality of the recording is sufficient for evaluation and the candidate’s performance meets the highest standards, clearly exceeding the admission threshold." In-person is preferred.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 7,700 per academic year for non-EU students on the Composition and Music Technology MA, 2026/2027 rate — the CHEAPEST credible studio-craft master found in the entire eight-country region. Across EAMT the range is quoted as EUR 1,500-14,000/yr depending on programme and EU/non-EU status. IMPORTANT: EAMT states "Full-time studies conducted in Estonian are tuition-free regardless of nationality" and its fee tables apply only to "study programs whose language of instruction is English" — so an Estonian-language route would be free, though the Composition and Music Technology MA’s availability in Estonian for a foreign student is UNVERIFIED.
otherFees: Non-refundable application fee EUR 75 (one source says EUR 70 — treat EUR 75 as current), normally by bank transfer. Application via DreamApply (estonia.dreamapply.com).
totalCostEstimate: Approx. EUR 15,400 tuition over 2 years + Tallinn living costs (Estonia is the cheapest cost-of-living country in this region; Estonian residence-permit subsistence requirement UNVERIFIED for 2027). Realistically EUR 30,000-35,000 all-in for the degree — an order of magnitude below Norway or Uniarts-in-English.
scholarships: "A limited number of scholarships are available for international students", with "auditions for the scholarships usually take place at the end of September" — i.e. AFTER the intake starts, so they cannot be relied on to fund year one. Value and coverage UNVERIFIED. Estonia also runs the Dora Plus / Estonian government scholarship schemes for international master students — applicability to EAMT UNVERIFIED. The Estonian-language tuition exemption is the more reliable lever if it can be accessed.

institution: RISEBA University of Applied Sciences, jointly with RTU Liepāja Academy (Liepājas Universitāte)
program: New Media and Audiovisual Art / Audiovisual and Immersive Technology Arts — Master. Joint programme; the Liepāja-based specialisation is "Skaņu māksla un elektroniskā mūzika" (Sound Art and Electronic Music)
accreditationStatus: Accredited Latvian higher education institution (RISEBA), joint programme with RTU Liepāja Academy
institutionType: Private university of applied sciences (RISEBA) in partnership with a public university academy
language: ENGLISH-TAUGHT (confirmed on the RISEBA programme page)
durationEcts: 120 ECTS / 2 years full-time. Based at Architecture and Media Centre H2O, Riga (Sound Art and Electronic Music strand delivered in Liepāja).
whatYouStudy: RISEBA’s current English page presents two thematic strands — Digital Storytelling and Interactive Narratives, and Immersive Technologies (XR Art, AI, Game Design) — and states that sound art and electronic music are integrated throughout the curriculum, particularly in the Audio Culture module, RATHER THAN being standalone specialisations. The four-specialisation description (Audiovisual Media Art and Multimedia Performing Arts in Riga; Digital Art and Sound Art and Electronic Music in Liepāja) comes from partner/third-party sources. The two descriptions conflict — the programme appears to have been restructured. UNVERIFIED which structure applies for 2027.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM-ish: applicants must hold a bachelor’s or equivalent diploma "in humanities, arts, or related fields", demonstrate "English language proficiency at least at the B2 level", submit a creative portfolio, pass an entrance examination, and submit a prospective master’s thesis project application.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the requirement is a bachelor "in humanities, arts, or related fields". A BSc Software Engineering is neither humanities nor arts; "or related fields" is undefined. UNVERIFIED, but for a media-technology programme an engineering degree is more plausibly "related" here than at any conservatoire in this list.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: a creative portfolio of "3-5 examples of audiovisual or new media work". No length or file-format specification is published — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: NO performance audition and NO ear-training test. There is an entrance examination (format UNVERIFIED) plus a prospective master’s thesis project proposal. Selection is portfolio- and project-driven.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 4,700 per year for students from countries outside the EU/EEA/candidate countries (EUR 4,100/yr for EU/EEA). That is EUR 9,400 for the full 120-ECTS master — the LOWEST published non-EU tuition of any programme found in this sweep.
totalCostEstimate: EUR 9,400 tuition + Riga living costs over 2 years — plausibly under EUR 25,000 all-in, the cheapest total in the region.
scholarships: None published on the programme page. UNVERIFIED.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — not listed on the programme page. Contact programme director Anna Viduleja, +371 26317874.
scopeNote: BORDERLINE / MOSTLY OUT OF SCOPE — the Liepāja strand is SOUND ART AND ELECTRONIC MUSIC, which the brief excludes, and the current Riga structure has folded sound into an "Audio Culture" module inside an XR/immersive-media master. Not a record-production degree. Recorded because it is English-taught, portfolio-only, non-music-friendly and by far the cheapest, so it remains a fallback worth an enquiry.

whatYouStudy: KARLSTAD (Musikhögskolan Ingesund): the only music master is "Konstnärlig master i musik" 120 hp — a CHAMBER MUSIC / Western classical performance degree (principal instrument 60 hp, ensemble 15 hp, professional and research preparation 15 hp, independent thesis 30 hp; instruments piano, voice, violin, viola, cello, double bass, guitar, flute, clarinet). Entry requires "a bachelor’s degree in music" and a färdighetsprov on the principal instrument submitted BY VIDEO (upload deadline 11 February 2026, 16:00 — PRIOR CYCLE). Karlstad’s music-production offering is a 180 hp BACHELOR (Musikproduktionsprogrammet) plus freestanding courses. NO production master. LULEÅ/PITEÅ: "Ljudteknik" (Audio Technology) is a 3-year, 180-credit BACHELOR covering music recording, broadcast, concert sound, film sound and mastering — LTU’s Department of Music and Media offers doctoral education in the subject but NO taught master in audio technology was found (UNVERIFIED whether one exists under another name). LINNAEUS: Musikproduktionsprogrammet and the Musik- och ljuddesignprogrammet (120 hp, distance, run jointly with Mittuniversitetet and Högskolan Dalarna) are FIRST-CYCLE. DALARNA: Ljud- och musikproduktionsprogrammet and Musik- och ljuddesign are FIRST-CYCLE (a third year yields a bachelor in Sound and Music Production). SÖDERTÖRN: no music-production programme at any level surfaced. SKÖVDE: Dataspelsutveckling - ljud and Dataspelsutveckling - musik are BACHELOR game-audio programmes; the four advanced-level programmes are Serious Games, Digitalt berättande: spel och kulturarv, Games User Experience and Spelutveckling — none is music production. MALMÖ ACADEMY OF MUSIC (Lund): the "Musikproducent" offering is a ONE-YEAR FREESTANDING COURSE (recording and studio technology, acoustics, music production, sequencing, music law, music and sound analysis, synthesis and mastering, mostly in Logic Pro with basic Pro Tools and analogue training), NOT a master. Lund’s music masters are Music Composition and Music Composition - Scoring for Film and Media (composition, out of scope). No music-production master.

program: FUNDING RECORD — Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP)
language: n/a
whatYouStudy: Funds a master’s degree at any Swedish university listed as eligible. This is THE decisive funding instrument for a Tunisian applying to Sweden, and it applies to KMH and KTH alike.
entryRequirements: Open to applicants from 41 eligible countries with demonstrated work and leadership experience. TUNISIA IS ON THE ELIGIBLE-COUNTRY LIST (confirmed across multiple secondary sources; the si.se page itself returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching and should be re-checked manually). Applicants must first apply to a Swedish master’s programme through universityadmissions.se in the January round, then apply separately to SI.

scholarshipName: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP)
scholarships: FULLY FUNDED: covers tuition fees, living expenses, travel grant and insurance. For Tunisian citizens specifically the travel grant is SEK 15,000 for the entire study period. The work-and-leadership-experience requirement is the real filter — a candidate straight out of a BSc with no professional record is weak for SISGP; documented professional work (including in software) strengthens it materially.
deadline: SI normally opens in early February and closes in late February, AFTER the mid-January university application deadline. Exact 2027 dates UNVERIFIED — the si.se page must be checked manually because it blocks automated access.
